answer: A harbor model gives every new identity a safe but narrow berth: small quotas and no influence until it proves itself. Trust then climbs like a terrace, each level unlocking only after verified work and time, and progress cannot be bought or transferred. A ledge guards every step: caught cheating and the identity falls off, losing its bond, its terrace and its history. A sybil attacker must therefore pay the full price of time, work and deposit for every single clone, while one honest identity climbs once.
